profilePeriod: MP and Restore Britain leader, 2024–30 September 2026; dated earlier context.
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

sources.title: Restore Civil Liberties
sources.evidence: Proposes repealing Online Safety Act, preventing future lockdowns, blocking compulsory digital ID, protecting self-defence, and investigating vaccine rollout. Party claims about vaccine harms are not independently medical findings.

sources.title: Make Britain Safe Again
sources.evidence: Supports stop and search, a binding death-penalty referendum, taxi CCTV, pepper spray and proscription of extremist Islamist organisations.

sources.title: Reverse Mass Immigration
sources.evidence: Seeks deportations encompassing some lawful residents, abolition of asylum system and mandatory detention of illegal entrants; permits easier spousal visas for selected countries under English and self-support conditions.

sources.title: Social and Cultural Foundations
sources.evidence: Supports Christian heritage teaching and church protection, family assistance, biological-sex law, reversing assisted dying and late-abortion changes, burqa ban and religious-slaughter restrictions. This does not establish opposition to every early abortion or same-sex relationship.

sources.title: Reward the Nation’s Grafters
sources.evidence: Advocates abolishing inheritance tax and IR35, low corporation tax, domestic investment incentives, remittance levy and conditional welfare with a vulnerable-citizen safety net.

sources.title: The Wealth of Our Nation
sources.evidence: Later economic paper proposes 19% corporation tax, abolishing inheritance tax and stamp duty, benefits and quango budget restraint, triple-lock reform and a smaller state over two Parliaments. Retrieved indexed full text after direct fetch timed out.

sources.title: Put British Interests First
sources.evidence: Advocates rearmament and use of military power where British interests require; alliances and aid assessed instrumentally, not as permanent commitments. This is assertive realism, not blanket pacifism.

sources.title: Safeguard Election Integrity
sources.evidence: Retains elections but restricts postal voting and foreign-national participation, with prosecution for fraud; universal adult-resident franchise cannot be assumed.

sources.title: Rebuild Industry, Infrastructure and Energy
sources.evidence: Supports countryside protection, energy sovereignty, prohibition of foreign ownership of energy infrastructure, fossil extraction, reservoirs and Tube automation.

sources.title: Energy Policy Paper
sources.evidence: Adds nuclear expansion including small modular reactors, emergency planning reform, domestic oil/gas and dynamic commercial electricity pricing.

sources.title: Quantitative Easing (Prohibition), Lowe speech
sources.evidence: Attacks QE, bailouts, deficits and state expansion; praises Milei and requires parliamentary authority for exceptional monetary expansion. Calls for government costs financed by transparent taxation, not abolition of all taxation.

sources.title: Lowe announces rolling back devolution, The National via inkl
sources.evidence: Reports Lowe’s 14 September announcement to reverse devolution and strengthen the Union; detailed paper still being developed. Direct quoted pledge and linked original post support direction, not an invented institutional blueprint.

sources.title: International Engagement, Commons official record
sources.evidence: Lowe asks why government has not considered a Commonwealth free-trade deal; distinguishes selective international trade support from unrestricted global integration.

sources.title: Restore Britain: is new far-right party a threat to Farage?, The Week
sources.evidence: Independent report corroborates rearmament, Christian-curriculum emphasis, speech-law repeal and referendum on capital punishment; situates Lowe’s harder migration position relative to Reform.

sources.title: Policing Policy Paper
sources.evidence: Proposes independent constables, democratic accountability boards without political operational control, national and regional training colleges and national criminal intelligence.

sources.title: Retaking the English Castle
sources.evidence: Defends jury trials, self-defence and repeal of Scotland’s hate-crime statute through Westminster powers.

sources.title: Join Us
sources.evidence: Party explicitly identifies direct democracy, traditional Christianity, low taxes and small government as principles.

sources.title: The Maverick Mandate bibliographic entry
sources.evidence: Biography of Lowe is authored by Brooke O Calloway, not Lowe, and therefore excluded.

sources.title: Patriot Games bibliographic entry
sources.evidence: Political book about Lowe and other right-wing figures is authored by Simon Tomlin, not Lowe, and therefore excluded.

facts: September devolution-reversal pledge strengthens the Union; February self-defence paper explicitly invokes Westminster over Scotland.
estrutura.tension: National legal sovereignty coexists with local scrutiny and independent constables; do not infer a single national police force.

facts: Direct democracy and death-penalty referendum are explicit; national elections remain central.
representacao.tension: Postal and citizenship voting restrictions plus hostility to judicial obstacles temper universalist participation; no evidence of ending elections.

facts: Digital-ID and censorship opposition sit beside searches, capital punishment and compulsory taxi CCTV.
poder.tension: Selective liberty for lawful citizens with strong coercion against offenders and migrants; no blanket libertarianism.

facts: Mandatory assimilation, reduced legal residence security and abolition of asylum; selected self-supporting spouses remain admissible.
imigracao.tension: Strong restriction is not prohibition of every migrant or every personal foreign custom.

facts: Rearmament and military leverage explicitly advocated in February platform.
diplomacia.tension: National-interest conditions limit overseas adventures without implying disarmament.

facts: Treats allies, aid, sanctions and deployments as instruments of British national interest.
intervencao.tension: Rejects universal obligations but keeps coercive external tools available.

facts: Protects inheritance and entrepreneurial ownership; August spending cuts fund tax cuts.
economia.tension: Retains a safety net and public sovereign functions; domestic energy ownership is distinct from nationalisation.

facts: Abolish IR35, cut tax, restrain budgets and prohibit routine QE.
controle.tension: Domestic incentives and remittance levy qualify laissez-faire; parliamentary control of QE differs from politicised routine rate setting.

facts: Commonwealth trade deal sought in 2024; 2026 excludes foreign ownership of energy infrastructure.
comercio.tension: Selective trading openness combines with productive sovereignty, not autarky or borderless global markets.

facts: Protects Christian national inheritance and church buildings; education framed as historical literacy.
religiao.tension: Christian public identity does not establish clerical supremacy or religious exemptions from ordinary law.

facts: Family policy, biological-sex recognition, assisted-dying opposition and reversal of late-abortion changes.
moral.tension: No verified blanket ban on early abortion or gay civil equality; avoid converting traditionalism into every possible restriction.

facts: Nuclear reactors and Tube automation supported alongside countryside protection.
tecnologia.tension: Industrial modernisation differs from embryo enhancement and unrestricted human augmentation; medical mandates also opposed.

uncertainties: Checked live sources on 2026-10-01; preserved the requested profile endpoint of 30 September 2026.
No existing answers, vectors, similarity reports or numerical results consulted before answering. Existing research used only for period and URLs.
Party platforms are evidence of public advocacy, not independently established accuracy of medical, demographic, crime or economic claims.

No direct policy verified on embryo intelligence enhancement, neural implants, all same-sex rights, early abortion, compulsory military service, or a complete federal tax settlement. Relevant answers will be explicitly reasoned analogies, not claimed quotations.
Detailed devolution plan was announced as forthcoming; local administrative delegation remains compatible with Union centralisation.
Brazilian questions treated as institutional analogies to Britain; not fabricated positions on specific Brazilian legislation.

validationReview: Reviewed 96.4% similarity to Tony Abbott and 95.4% to Flavio Bolsonaro. Shared conservative, market and national-identity positions are expected. Lowe has a distinct parliamentary/devolution context, monetary policy, gun-ownership policy, religious programme and technology evidence. Technology neutrals identify explicit value tensions rather than claims of personal answers to undocumented hypotheticals.

independentAudit.validation: Independent review complete. User requested retaining the full 32-person scope after the overlap report; current upstream validator results are recorded separately.

bookDecision.reason: No self-authored qualifying political book verified. Dedicated general author/book, memoir and WorldCat-targeted searches found biographies and political books by other authors, plus party policy papers; authorship criteria prevent substituting those. No existing books entry.

religionMetadataReview.reason: Public Christian commitments form part of the documented political or religious position; this is not inferred from ancestry or the vector.
